source_text: Haec ita dispecta totum ordinem dei iudicis operarium et, ut dignius dixerim, protectorem catholicae et summae illius bonitatis ostendunt, quam (ut) semotam a iudiciariis sensibus et in suo statu puram nolunt Marcionitae in eodem deo agnoscere, pluente super bonos et malos et solem suum oriri faciente super iustos et iniustos, quod alius deus omnino non praestat. nam etsi hoc quoque testimonium Christi in creatorem Marcion. de euangelio eradere ausus est, sed ipse mundus inscriptus est et omni a conscientia legitur. et erit haec ipsa patientia creatoris in iudicium Marcionis, illa patientia, quae expectat paenitentiam potius peccatoris quam mortem et mauult misericordiam quam sacrificium, auertens destinatum iam exitium Niniuitis et largiens spatium uitae Ezechiae lacrimis et restituens statum regni Babylonis tyranno paenitentia functo: illam dico misericordiam, quae et filium Saulis moriturum ex deuotione populo concessit et Dauid delicta in domum Uriae confessum uenia liberauit et ipsum Israhel totiens restituit quotiens iudicauit, totiens refouit quotiens et increpuit.
pass_a_gloss: These things having been thus disregarded show the whole order of God the judge and, that I may say it more worthily, the protector of the catholic and highest goodness, which the Marcionites do not want to recognize in the same God, as separated from judicial senses and in its own state pure, raining upon good and evil and making its sun rise upon just and unjust, which another God altogether does not provide. For even if Marcion dared to erase this testimony of Christ from the creator from the gospel, the world itself is inscribed and is read by every conscience. And this patience of the creator will be in judgment against Marcion, that patience which waits for the repentance of the sinner rather than death and prefers mercy to sacrifice, turning away the destined destruction of the Ninevites and granting a space of life to Hezekiah with tears and restoring the state of the kingdom of Babylon to the tyrant who has performed repentance: I say that mercy, which also granted the son of Saul to die from devotion to the people and freed David from guilt, confessed in the house of Uriah, with free pardon and restored Israel itself as many times as it judged, as many times it comforted as it also rebuked.

pass_b_english: Disregarding these facts reveals the entire order of God the Judge and, to put it more worthily, the guardian of that catholic and supreme goodness which the Marcionites refuse to recognize in the same God — a goodness kept pure and separate from judicial categories — because he rains on the good and the evil and makes his sun rise on the just and the unjust (Matt 5:45), something another god altogether fails to provide. Even if Marcion dared to cut this testimony of Christ about the Creator out of the Gospel, the world itself is written with it, and every conscience reads it. This patience of the Creator will stand in judgment against Marcion — the patience that waits for the sinner's repentance rather than death and prefers mercy to sacrifice, turning aside the doom decreed for the Ninevites (Jonah 3:4-10), granting Hezekiah an extension of life through his tears (2 Kings 20:1-6), and restoring the Babylonian tyrant's kingdom after he repented. I mean that mercy which also let Saul's son die out of devotion to the people, and freed David from his guilt — confessed in Uriah's house — with full pardon, and restored Israel as often as it judged it, as often as it comforted it even while rebuking it.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the necessary biblical citations for the allusions (Matt 5:45, Jonah 3:4-10, 2 Kings 20:1-6) which were present in the sense of the Latin but not explicitly cited in the source text, fulfilling the requirement for added identifications. Pass A and B are consistent with the Locked Latin.
